D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the full cybersecurity engineering stack with depth: secure Python scripting, Linux hardening, secure Django REST API, OWASP Top 10, Burp Suite, JWT/OAuth2, Docker, AWS, and a CI/CD DevSecOps pipeline. Each month has explicit interview prep goals tied to the month's technical content, and the capstone is a fully deployed, containerized, cloud-native application with documented security testing. Plan 2 covers similar topics but at a shallower depth — it introduces Metasploit and CTFs which are more pentesting-oriented than software engineering-oriented, and its project work is vague ('a secure Python/Django application or a security-focused Python tool'). Plan 2's interview prep is concentrated in Month 6 only, whereas Plan 1 distributes it across all months. Plan 1's portfolio deliverables are concrete, employer-worthy, and progressively built; Plan 2's are loosely defined and lack deployment specifics. Plan 1 is clearly stronger on hiring readiness.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 has a concrete, deployed capstone with CI/CD security gates, distributed interview prep, and role-aligned portfolio deliverables every month, versus Plan 2's vague project scope and back-loaded interview preparation.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility

This is transparent and well-managed. Plan 2 provides a daily breakdown (1.5h theory, 1.5h practice, 1h project/DSA) but does not track total hours or buffer. Plan 1's Month 5 asks the user to learn Docker, AWS security, DevSecOps, CI/CD, SAST, and incident response in one month — this is ambitious but not unreasonable given the 84-hour budget. Plan 2 introduces Metasploit, OpenVAS, and CTFs in Month 4 alongside Python scripting and three major tools, which is cognitively dense. Both plans have some overloading, but Plan 1's explicit hour tracking and buffer management make it more feasible in practice.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 1 explicitly tracks total hours, allocates buffer, and breaks down monthly time budgets, making feasibility transparent and manageable, while Plan 2 has no hour accounting or buffer planning.
